question: Within the same published Karel program, how often does copying a demonstrated primitive-action schedule onto a different input world reach the recorded target world? Can different schedules reach an identical endpoint?
data: Prefer the MSR-Redmond/Devlin-Bunel published synthetic test split and report the human challenge separately if directly accessible. Never train, sample on outcomes, or combine splits. If these files are unavailable, use an explicitly named real author-released Karel benchmark with multiple worlds and reference code. A single-input example cannot identify within-program transfer.
cohort: Use all supplied programs in the chosen bounded evaluation split, up to the first 2500 records in released order if larger. For each program evaluate the first six paired worlds, or all if fewer. Report counts for records with fewer than two worlds separately; do not copy across programs.
primary: Leave each selected world out in turn as target. Evaluate every remaining source world's complete primitive trace as open-loop commands on the target input. Illegal action fails. Score exact recorded terminal grid including pose, obstacles and marker counts; independently score literal primitive trace equality. Average across source choices for each target, targets for each program, then programs equally. A recorded trace, or traced reference program when traces are absent, must produce its own recorded output on every included input. Stop on reference mismatch.
secondary: For k=1,3,5 support traces when eligible, average over every size-k subset of the other worlds. Compare outcome-blind most frequent exact trace (average ties uniformly) with the retrospective ceiling from choosing any successful candidate. Average using the same program/target weighting for mutually eligible samples and report denominator for each k. Hindsight is an availability ceiling, not a router. Decompose endpoint success into identical trace versus different successful trace. Compare programs with and without data-dependent syntax and programs with identical vs varying observed traces. For shared executed prefix lengths 1 and 3, condition on source and target traces sharing that exact prefix and both having a subsequent action. Count matching next actions and terminal replay success with explicit coverage. Prefix results are ordered-pair descriptive counts, not causal evidence.
scope: The open-loop selector sees the program group and support traces; query input is supplied only to the replay simulator. An agent seeing the complete query world and known deterministic program could execute or plan the exact schedule before acting. This tests fixed trace sharing, neither online necessity nor hierarchy. Use no outcome-dependent filtering, task solving model or new GPU jobs.

source_recovery_before_outcomes.original_download: Public MSR OneDrive zip redirected to HTTP 403; the nearai authors' historical S3 archive returned 404. No original test or challenge bytes were available from these endpoints.
source_recovery_before_outcomes.corroboration_rule: Require all 1000 published short validation-program token strings to appear in the recovered programs. Independently replay every supplied own-world action trace to its exact recorded output. Report order alignment and explicitly limit provenance of input/outputs to the identified mirror.
source_recovery_before_outcomes.authored_case: Evaluate all 3 published pre/post worlds of karel-stairway separately, tracing its released AST on each. Alternative NeurTaskSyn synthetic test split has 103 single-world and 1 missing-task program, so cannot itself support within-program pairs.
